ai_disclosure: In our game development process, we have adopted AI technology to generate art content, mainly for the character portraits of esports players and illustrations in game events. We hope to provide players with richer and more diverse character portraits, but considering the economic, manpower, and time aspects, we find it difficult to afford a large amount of hand-drawn content. We have tried to separate parts such as the mouth, face, and nose, and then assemble them into 3D characters, but the effect was not satisfactory. Therefore, we decided to try a new method: using AI to generate these contents. We used some of the content we had created before to train the AI model, allowing it to learn and understand the art style and requirements we want. Now, all the AI-generated character portraits and illustrations in the game are made by our trained model, and after completion, we also manually correct them. We deeply understand that AI cannot replace the creativity and uniqueness of real artists. For this, we feel very sorry, but we also promise you that “Esports Godfather” is not a work without sincerity. We have spent a tremendous amount of time polishing innovative gameplay and various experience content. In these four and a half years, we have been committed to completing a work that satisfies everyone. We hope you can understand our decision and continue to support our game. We will continue to work hard to provide you with a better gaming experience.

ai_disclosure: In our game development process, we have adopted AI technology to generate art content, mainly for the character portraits of esports players and illustrations in game events. We hope to provide players with richer and more diverse character portraits, but considering the economic, manpower, and time aspects, we find it difficult to afford a large amount of hand-drawn content. We have tried to separate parts such as the mouth, face, and nose, and then assemble them into 3D characters, but the effect was not satisfactory. Therefore, we decided to try a new method: using AI to generate these contents. We used some of the content we had created before to train the AI model, allowing it to learn and understand the art style and requirements we want. Now, all the AI-generated character portraits and illustrations in the game are made by our trained model, and after completion, we also manually correct them. We deeply understand that AI cannot replace the creativity and uniqueness of real artists. For this, we feel very sorry, but we also promise you that “Esports Godfather” is not a work without sincerity. We have spent a tremendous amount of time polishing innovative gameplay and various experience content. In these four and a half years, we have been committed to completing a work that satisfies everyone. We hope you can understand our decision and continue to support our game. We will continue to work hard to provide you with a better gaming experience.

name: Shadowtime
ai_disclosure: The team utilised AI due to the thematic relevance of the story. This application marks the first use of AI in creating 3D and 6DOF environments that morph seamlessly into one another in VR. This innovative technique is showcased in a short sequence within the experience. Based in Utrecht, Institute of Time  is an interdisciplinary film and new media company specializing in documentary films and XR experiences. Focusing on creative projects around climate change, it aims to bring a different perspective to our current life and uncertain future with storytelling. "Shadowtime" is a hand-tracking experience designed specifically for PC-linked Meta Quest 2 headset. Graphic Quality: To achieve optimal graphic quality, ensure that an h265 codec is installed on your PC. "Shadowtime" will run properly even if you don't have all these settings.

ai_disclosure: # AI Usage in Our Game In our game, we have utilized generative artificial intelligence (AI) technology to enhance certain aspects of the visual experience. Specifically, we have employed AI-powered tools to assist in the creation of some background images and textures. Key points about our AI usage: 1. **Pre-rendered Content**: The AI-generated elements are pre-rendered during the development process. This means that the images you see in the game are not being created in real-time as you play. 2. **Limited Scope**: AI has been used primarily for non-essential background elements and textures. All main characters, story-critical environments, and core gameplay elements are hand-crafted by our artists. 3. **Human Oversight**: While AI tools have been used to generate initial ideas or base images, our art team carefully reviews, edits, and refines all AI-assisted content to ensure it meets our quality standards and fits seamlessly into the game's aesthetic. 4. **No Live Generation**: Our game does not use AI to generate any content during gameplay. All AI-assisted elements are fixed and do not change dynamically. 5. **Copyright Compliance**: We have taken great care to ensure that all AI-generated content is original and does not infringe on existing copyrights. Our use of AI tools is in compliance with their terms of service and licensing agreements. We believe that the thoughtful use of AI in our development process has allowed us to create richer, more detailed environments for players to explore, while maintaining the artistic integrity and vision of our game. As always, we welcome player feedback and are committed to providing a high-quality gaming experience.

ai_disclosure: This project was initiated in September 2022. To avoid the misuse of generative AI tools, only the default datasets provided by the respective tools were used during development. The methods of use included: 1. Processing real photographs to create "alien" or "distorted" visual effects; 2. Using abstract images generated from provided keywords as references for manual redesign, reconstruction, and painting; 3. Generating atmospheric music clips by adjusting parameters such as instrumentation and tempo, followed by manual editing and refinement. All content involving artificial intelligence was completed before 2023. Since then, the use of AI image generation technology in development has been fully discontinued and will not continue in future production. For all AI-generated image assets used in this work, only usage rights are retained by the project.

ai_disclosure: All of the images in this game are generated by neural networks trained on images (aka “AI generated”). If you choose to boycott all AI generated material, please do not buy this game. If you are uncomfortable with the thought but are interested in my game, please read on. The aesthetic of this game had to come from the strange, uncanny look of AI. There is a heartlessness to the visuals that is intentional. I am not trying to copy the look of other artists. The only tool capable of producing the look I was going for was a malfunctioning AI. Ironically, I have had a number of people tell me that it looks much more realistic than standard AI. I am assuming this is because of how I tried to reproduce the look of old media. All images, aside from the title screen, credits and some of the video shot on camcorder were generated by AI prompts. It took several days of exploring before I began generating images that fit the aesthetic I was looking for. I have heard AI described as a slot machine, and I think the metaphor is somewhat accurate. I think of this as similar to indeterminacy in music. Using random number generators can produce interesting outputs, but you need to refine and direct the system to do so. I started my process in Midjourney. My ratio of usable images was around 100 to 1; for every 100 images I generated, I found one usable piece for the game. I created an automated process to transform these images to 16:9 widescreen in Photoshop Beta. Some of these images I touched up manually or regenerated sections of the image. There are some real images and hand painted imagery within the AI elements. Often, I would have to generate the sides of the image multiple times because photoshop didn’t generate what I needed. To those concerned about not paying artists: I understand this, but I want to be clear that this was not created to replace the work of artists, any more than the synthesized scores to horror films were about replacing orchestras. ai_disclosure: At Lovely Bytes, we're not just developers, we're passionate gamers like you. And because we understand the gamer's perspective, we firmly believe that the heart of a truly great game lies in the emotional depth and authenticity that only human creativity can provide. In the development of UNHEIM, artificial intelligence plays a supporting role to accelerate our production, and is used mindfully to help us with certain time-consuming tasks, such as visual brainstorming, or speeding up the process of creating some of the textures. Additionally, AI bravely tackles the Herculean task of turning our chaotic creative thoughts and wild brainstorming scribbles into something resembling coherent, actionable documents. Our approach to AI is to use it as a tool to augment our skills and capabilities, not to substitute the craft elements that are crucial for creating a deeply engaging and memorable game experience. ai_disclosure: NO AI WAS USED IN THE CREATION OF ANY ART ASSETS, MUSIC OR WRITING. AI IS ONLY USED FOR CHARACTER INTERACTIONS AND MECHANICS. All AI models are run on the user's machine using their GPU. No data usage is sent to us and the game can be played offline. The AI is character-based. Each character has their own model and will respond and react to player interaction in a specific way, each providing a unique challenge. As the player progresses through the year in Millennium Whisper, they will build relationships with the characters as all interactions are fed to the models and the characters rate their affection levels towards the player. The challenge comes from the player needing to juggle their social relationship with all the characters at once as characters have the ability to communicate with eachother by spreading rumours thereby allowing neglected characters to sabotage the player's relationship with other characters. The characters will also accept or reject date invites from the player or author their own date invitations. At the end of the game the AIs evaluates which character the player ends up with.

ai_disclosure: FACEMINER is a concept-driven game that directly engages with the ethics of AI. For thematic purposes, the game features faces which have been generated by a GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) trained on the FFHQ dataset, a research dataset released by NVIDIA that is the backbone of many real-world facial recognition applications. name: Brix Infinite
ai_disclosure: I use a highly curated AI prompt, driven by automation software, to generate levels for the game.    By taking an AI prompt that describes the basic architecture of a level, and adding the difficulty and a theme description, I get back an 8x20 grid.  I then run a post process bit of code that looks for errors, and re-generates the level if an error is found. I also use a highly curated AI prompt,  driven by automation software, to generate new avatars. Again, I add a theme (e.g. cute baby animals dressed as pirates) plus a list of about 260 animals to generate the base avatars.  I then run image processing to remove the background and create a variety of sizes.  Finally, I look at each avatar individually and edit to finalize removal of the background if anything was missed, or even redo the background removal manually if it got messed up by the automated image processor.

While AI has been a valuable tool in streamlining these aspects of development, the core design, storytelling, and gameplay mechanics of Duskmarch are crafted by me, reflecting my passion for creating an immersive and engaging experience. ai_disclosure: AI was used in the creation of certain visual assets, including character avatars, title screen artwork, promotional materials, and background art. However, these assets still required substantial manual work such as design, sketching, outline drawing, and polishing. The AI was used primarily as a tool for coloring and enhancement, and it did not dictate the creative direction. The visual style remains faithful to the original Little Fighter 2. Some people assume that because AI was used in certain artwork, it must have been applied throughout the entire project. That is far from the truth. I used AI primarily for large-scale visual tasks. To give a clearer picture: the game includes over 3,000 hand-crafted sprite frames, composed from thousands of hand-drawn body parts. In contrast, only about 100 images were AI-assisted, and many of those, such as promotional artwork, don't even appear in the actual game. I understand that some people may have concerns about the use of AI in the creative process. But I hope people can see the broader context and appreciate the amount of manual effort that went into making this game. Please know that I’m a solo developer working with a limited budget. I’ve been developing this project for around 3.5 years; even quitting my full-time job for a year to work on it full time, without expecting it to cover even half of my previous salary. I've done my best to balance quality and practicality. Your understanding and support mean a great deal to me.

ai_disclosure: Beneath The Six features an AI narrator who serves as a dungeon master to guide you and comment on your experiences in the daily generated content. We commissioned actor Tom Canton (The Witcher TV series) to record a library of dialogue. This was then used by ElevenLabs to train the AI voice. Both Magicave and ElevenLabs have a commitment to ensuring the rights of voice actors are protected. Magicave has assigned ownership of the AI voice to Tom Canton, licensing it from him for use in the game, while allowing him the freedom to use his AI voice in other media – whether games, voiceovers, animations, audiobooks or movies (https://www.gamewatcher.com/news/beneath-the-six-turn-based-roguelike). Each day we generate new daily content for the dungeon and arena. As part of this we pass the generation data to an LLM to create dialogue for the AI narrator so they can comment on the content included for that day. Some of the daily generated content for the arena and dungeon modes use an LLM to create names for two other purposes. One is for creating the name of any Champion enemies which appear in the dungeon. The other is for creating a name for the daily arena run.

name: Celestial DEUS + Aleatores Palace
ai_disclosure: As a solo developer, transparency with my players is essential to me. That's why I want to clarify that I have used artificial intelligence tools to assist in the creative process of Celestial Deus. Working alone on a project of this scope requires finding creative solutions. AI allowed me to bring my artistic vision to life where my own skills or resources were limited. Here is how it was used: Skybox: The skybox, which depicts a stylized sky filled with large clouds as if viewed from a great height, was generated by an AI to match the game's unique atmosphere. Voice Acting: To bring the characters to life, I first recorded all their voices myself. Then, I used an AI to transform my voice recordings, ensuring that each voice perfectly matches the personality and character of the deity it represents. Music: I composed the foundational music tracks myself, and then used AI to remix and enhance them. This gave them more style and complexity for a more immersive ambiance. My approach was always to use my own creations as a starting point and guide these tools, allowing me to deliver a more complete experience than I could have achieved on my own.

ai_disclosure: - 1 of the 8 optional title themes is alleged to have used AI - even though the band insists otherwise, offered up the track a year before this project existed, and refused any payment for doing so. You can interrogate them on the matter here: https://www.bandlab.com/track/390bf936d0be49dda14dd68c125d500f_2a98d8102c85406ab4e8fdfbfe0cbda5 Had I used AI myself, I like to think I'd take the opportunity to produce something more relevant than muttering "there are people who will never change" on a loop. The intention was to create an "other-worldly" art style that is deliberately distinct from the developer's own 2D or 3D. ai_disclosure: As the AI debate continues to evolve I feel the need to add nuance to this statement so players can make an informed decision whether or not to support human game developers. I took 5 years of classes learning code and 3D to produce my game.  When the AI boom hit, Tobiano was already a functioning breeding and management simulator.  At my day job, we were encouraged to use AI for everything from image generation to writing emails.  I opposed the use of AI for creative aspects and human communication, but tested out chatbots for help with code.  Problems solved with AI include things like "how do i make the camera follow the player".  A lot of the problems ended up more convoluted by AI. Most of the code written early in the game has gone through 2-3 iterations to simplify and be easier to work with and debug. For example, the riding lesson system was redone completely after the first 5 lessons were added, just to make the next 5 lessons easier for me to add.  Building a large and complex game requires understanding of code and the developer needs to know where to find every method, every variable.  There is an important distinction between "hey Claude, build me a horse game" and saving a couple hours writing a database. I've spent literally thousands of hours writing code for my passion project. AI use in the game today consists of time-saving things like "add these markings to this list". AI can be useful for debugging, when the root of a problem can be a simple typo that is hard to spot. Bigger debugging problems always require a broader conceptual understanding of the way the game is set up and take human hours to solve. AI has not been used to create any 3D assets, textures, audio, or writing or translations in the game. I cannot guarantee that people I hire to do these tasks do not use AI, as these cooperations are based on trust. Placeholder AI-generated assets have been created for the Steam store splash images, with the intent of commissioning an artist if this gains community support. All in-game assets (sprites, music, sound effects, UI elements, and interactive content) were created by humans and are credited in the game credits. This is the third iteration of development, that was originally developed in 2019 with HTML + JS, then rebuilt in Unity, and then transferred to LOVE2D written in Lua. It was more-or-less built with a box of scraps in a cave in its first iterations, and modern software since those days have effectively blurred the line where task automation meets unethical AI consumption. It's up to each of us to determine where that line is for ourselves in a rapidly changing digital age. As both a solo game dev and multimedia artist carrying a full-time job in neither of those fields, I feel that it's important to be educating ourselves on where AI can be a useful tool to allow new opportunities and expand capabilities for independent creators that are otherwise untenable, while keeping the human side of game dev at its core, especially in the indie genre.

Its role is strictly limited to providing visual references, aesthetic guidance, and starting points to help our team work more efficiently. This approach allows us to maintain a strong and authentic artistic identity while benefiting from a more fluid, inspiring, and innovative creation process — directly reflected in the quality, coherence, and originality of our game.

ai_disclosure: AI-Generated Content Disclosure I am a solo developer with no programming background. Before using AI, I spent three months following YouTube tutorials, deleted everything and restarted three times, and typed every line of code myself until the foundation of this game clicked. From there, I used AI — primarily Claude — as a teacher and debugging partner across 7,000+ conversations over 16 months to learn GDScript and build every system in the game. The first line in my prompts is always "Stop being a yes sayer and always be brutal and honest." Here is exactly what AI was and wasn't used for: Code: I spent my first three months writing every line of code by hand. As the project grew, AI became a development partner — drafting code from my descriptions, which I then reviewed, debugged, and integrated. AI taught me programming concepts and helped me solve problems. Every design decision and system architecture is mine. Art: AI-generated with extensive human direction and manual editing. Some pieces required 15 pages of descriptions. I often assemble final art from multiple elements — finding references, combining parts, and making hands-on edits until it matches my vision. Animation: The first 14 enemies and 2 bosses were animated by me personally in DragonBones. For newer content, I'm exploring AI-generated animations and working to make them feel personal and consistent with the game's style — you can see examples with the later bosses. Some of these I'm still not satisfied with and will redo, which is just part of the process. Music: I produced 350+ tracks using AI music tools and curated the best for the game. All creative direction — mood, style, placement — is mine. Writing: All card text, lore, descriptions, and UI text are written by me. AI occasionally helps with polish. Game Design: Every mechanic, card interaction, and balance decision comes from a lifetime of gaming — hundreds of board games, decades of Magic: The Gathering, a career at Blizzard Entertainme

ai_disclosure: AI is used to generate the voices and advice of two opposing royal advisers (Left and Right Councillor). Each turn they comment on the situation and recommend different actions. If the player’s decree aligns more closely with one adviser’s stance, that adviser’s credibility increases while the other’s decreases. As the credibility gap grows, public trust is affected, reflecting rising factional tension. If an adviser’s credibility reaches zero, they resign—sometimes angrily—warning the player not to dismiss their counsel. The vacant seat is then filled by a successor adviser, represented by a different local LLM model. This creates shifting personalities and advice styles across runs. AI does not determine the game’s outcomes. Core consequences and metric changes are resolved by the game’s rule system; AI provides narrative and guidance within that system. If the game crashes, please blame the algorithm, as our "lead developer" is actually just a prompt engineer. - Music & Sound: The background tracks were generated by synthetic audio engines to ensure a continuous stream of procedurally generated slop-lofi beats. ai_disclosure: No AI-generated artwork, 3D models, animations, programming code, story content, or music are used in the game. Other assets were created in collaboration with artists or sourced from appropriately labelled, non-AI-generated content available through the official Fab marketplace. The story, storytelling, dialogue, game design, programming, and music were created by me as the developer. No content is generated live by AI during gameplay. I personally do not support games whose creative content is produced largely or entirely through generative AI. Voice generation was used only as a limited technical tool and did not replace the creative development or the work involved in building the game itself.

I'm an ordinary gamer who has played games for almost twenty years and always dreamed of making one of my own. But I can't write code, and I've never been trained in art or music. This game exists because generative AI filled those gaps for me: parts of the code were written with the help of AI coding tools; some character, environment, and UI art was created with image-generation models, then hand-picked and adjusted by me; some animation, music, and sound effects were also made with AI tools. Everything that makes it an actual game, though — the design, the balancing, the game feel, and every "is this fun?" decision — was done by me, across hundreds of playtests. The game contains no live-generated AI content. For me, AI wasn't an assembly line making a game in my place. It's what let an ordinary player finally build the game he'd been dreaming about. I hope some of that comes through when you play — and I'd genuinely welcome your feedback.

name: Wizard Disaster
ai_disclosure: Wizard Disaster was made by a solo developer, using generative AI tools as part of the production pipeline. Art. Character, boss and background artwork, and the source frames the animations are built from, were produced with generative image and video tools. Everything was then cut, keyed, aligned, retimed and composited by hand into the sheets the game actually plays. The generated output is the raw material, not the finished asset. Concept passes were made the same way. Audio. The music and most of the sound effects were generated with Suno, then trimmed, pitched, levelled and fitted to the length of the action each one accompanies. Not all of the audio is generated: a number of the effects are synthesised procedurally in code from a 1930s orchestra-pit palette, and the wizard's own voice (his cries and shouts) are human recordings. Code. Generative AI was used as a programming assistant during development, and to build and run the automated test harnesses that measure boss pacing, damage output and medal times. Those harnesses are development-only tooling and are not part of the shipped game. The game contains no live-generated AI content. Nothing is generated while you play, and the game makes no network or AI service calls at runtime.

name: Star Corsairs: Fractured Frontier
ai_disclosure: I'm not a professional game developer or artist. Making my own game had been a dream for years, but I never knew how to turn that dream into reality. Generative AI became the tool that finally made it possible. With its help, I created many of the game's visual and audio assets, including item, UI, skill, and module icons, character portraits, ships, space stations, backgrounds, the game icon, the Steam store artwork, and some of the sound effects. It also assisted me with programming. But Star Corsairs is not a game that AI simply generated. Every asset was reviewed, rejected, refined, or replaced until it matched the vision I had in mind. Every gameplay system was designed, tested, and reworked repeatedly until it felt right. The economy, ship balance, pirate AI, combat, and progression were all shaped through countless hours of playtesting and manual iteration. The story, world, and all of the writing were created by me. Without generative AI, this game would probably never have existed. But without the countless creative decisions, revisions, and work behind every part of it, Star Corsairs wouldn't exist either.

name: EQUILIBRIUM
ai_disclosure: EQUILIBRIUM uses generative AI to power its core gameplay mechanic: the Policy Terminal. LIVE-GENERATED CONTENT When a player types a directive or law in natural language (e.g., "Abolish the luxury car tax"), the AI Engine analyzes the request in real time and generates a structured governmental dossier, including: - Legislative feasibility analysis - Budget impact and financial coverage - Macroeconomic effects (GDP, debt, inflation) - Social and political consensus projections - Parliamentary vote simulation Model used: Anthropic Claude, accessed via API. Guardrails: AI output is constrained to a fixed set of structured fields defined by the developer. All numeric effects are clamped within bounds enforced by the simulation engine, so no AI output can produce values outside the game's defined ranges. The model operates only on the simulation state provided to it and cannot invent game data: commands that cannot be mapped to a valid government action are refused, and the player is offered bounded policy alternatives instead. No image, audio, or user-data generation is involved, and no player data is used to train any model. Because responses are generated at runtime, outputs vary between playthroughs: the same directive may produce different wording and different outcomes. PRE-GENERATED CONTENT The game's background music track was generated using AI tools during development and ships with the game.

name: Brainrot Simulator
ai_disclosure: We integrate artificial intelligence solely as a creative assistance tool during pre-production and artistic exploration phases. Specifically, we use image generators to produce preliminary concept art, explore different visual directions, and accelerate iteration on our graphic ideas. AI serves only as a source of inspiration, while the entire final content is fully created, curated, and refined by our human team. Generated images are never used as-is in the final product. Every visual element in the game (textures, characters, environments, illustrations, etc.) is recreated, retouched, painted, recomposed, or manually validated by our artists to ensure: originality of the content, respect for copyright, artistic consistency, and compliance with Steam/Valve guidelines. AI does not contribute to the generation of final assets, 3D models, animations, sounds, or any other elements directly integrated into the game. Its role is strictly limited to providing visual references, aesthetic guidance, and starting points to help our team work more efficiently. This approach allows us to maintain a strong and authentic artistic identity while benefiting from a more fluid, inspiring, and innovative creation process — directly reflected in the quality, coherence, and originality of our game.

name: Aika Was Supposed to Die
ai_disclosure: Hi everyone. I want to be open about how this game was made and why generative AI was used. Aika Was Supposed to Die began as a story that I wrote and developed over more than two years. The world, characters, dialogue, themes, and narrative direction were all written by me. I cared deeply about this story, and eventually I felt that a visual novel would be the best way to bring it to life. As an independent developer working with a limited budget, hiring a full team of artists is not financially possible for me right now. I greatly value human-made art and the work of professional artists. I am also a 3D artist who works with Unreal Engine, so this is something I genuinely care about. Rather than leave the story untold, I chose to use generative AI as part of the visual production process. The game’s images and video assets were created with the assistance of generative AI tools. However, I did not want that to become an excuse for delivering something careless or low-quality. In fact, having access to these tools encouraged me to be as ambitious as possible with the project. I created and refined a large number of images and animated sequences to give the game a richer and more cinematic presentation. Every asset was carefully directed, selected, edited, revised, and manually integrated into the story, with the goal of providing players with a cohesive, polished, and emotionally engaging experience. The writing, narrative design, scene direction, timing, editing, and final creative decisions were all handled by humans. Generative AI was used as a production tool, not as a replacement for authorship, creative direction, or care. No AI content is generated during gameplay. Optionally, Windows players can connect their own API key from OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini) or xAI (Grok) in Settings instead. Only while this option is on, the player's chat messages, recent chat history, saved chat memories and the character's profile are sent directly from the player's PC to the selected provider to generate replies, under that provider's terms (for example, Google may use chats sent through Gemini's free tier to improve its products), and usage is billed to the player's own account. The key is encrypted by Windows and stored only on the player's PC. It is never sent to WhyDuck Studio. Players can delete the key or switch back to the local model at any time. Characters are designed to follow developer-written personalities and content safety rules intended for all-ages conversations, whichever model is used. AI generates chat text only. ai_disclosure: Ammerow: Lands Beyond was developed with substantial AI assistance under human direction, selection and review. The music was created with Claude Compose, a bespoke composition system built for this project. Anthropic’s Claude assisted by writing and running code that arranges melody, harmony, counterpoint and orchestration note by note. The compositions were rendered using licensed virtual instruments in Ableton Live, then analysed and refined. No generative-audio or generative-music model was used. Every piece was directed, reviewed and approved by a human. The sound effects are an original, human-directed procedural synthesis library. Claude Code assisted in writing custom Python digital-signal-processing software and individual cue recipes. Waveforms were deterministically rendered from mathematical models and recorded seeds. No recordings, performers, samples, stock audio, sample libraries or generative-audio service were used to create the effects. Ammerow is designed primarily as a coloured ASCII game. Detailed creature, item and shopkeeper illustrations began as AI-generated source images, selected and reviewed under human direction, then converted through a deterministic ASCII-art pipeline. The optional Hybrid presentation offers 32×32 and 64×64 sprites made by cropping and sampling those same source illustrations. Neither conversion process uses additional image generation, but both retain their AI-generated source provenance. Terrain and subjects without sprite bindings use ordinary ASCII glyphs; inspection cards and shopkeepers retain their ASCII illustrations. No inherited Angband tilesets are included. Some narrative, gameplay data and other player-facing material were developed with AI assistance under human direction and review. AI coding assistants also contributed to the game’s software and production tools. Some Steam marketing backgrounds were created using OpenAI image-generation tools, then selected, reviewed and combined with deterministic Amm

ai_disclosure: Serv-Bot's Firewall uses AI tools in its art and media pipeline, always under human direction and review: Sprite art. The game's original hand-authored sprites were upscaled and repainted at native resolution with an image-editing model (Qwen-Image-Edit), then reviewed, corrected and in many cases restored to the originals by hand. Concept art for the six "arsenal" enemy types, the Serv-Bot HUD portraits and the achievement icon motifs were generated with local image models (Z-Image Turbo, Qwen-Image-Edit) from our own designs and reference art, then composited and finished in code. Canon elements such as the Greeb ship in the icons are the game's own sprite art, not generated. Cutscenes. The in-game story videos come from our SIGNAL series. Keyframes were generated with a local image model trained on our own characters, motion with a local video model (Wan 2.2), narration with a text-to-speech model (Kokoro) and music with local music models (ACE-Step, Stable Audio Open). Scripts, story, character designs, editing and direction are ours. Localization. Interface text in 28 languages was machine-translated with an AI model from our English source and has not yet been reviewed by native speakers. Code. Parts of the game's code were written with AI coding assistance, reviewed and tested by the developer. Sound effects are procedurally synthesised, not AI-generated. All AI generation ran on the developer's own hardware; no copyrighted third-party works were used as inputs beyond our own assets and characters.

Technical Implementation & Privacy: Local AI generation runs on the player’s device and supports offline single-player. Cloud AI requires an internet connection and uses credits. Safety & Moderation: We have implemented a multi-layered safety strategy to ensure a safe experience: Model-Level Guardrails: The included local model is an Instruct model with built-in safety measures. System-Level Directives: All prompts include an additional safety layer to prevent sexual violence, pedophilia, minor abuse/exploitation, explicit sexual behavior, or hate speech. Gameplay Integration: While the primary Visual Novel is hand-authored, the results of your sandbox evaluations influence the story's trajectory. The AI serves as a tool for narrative exploration, bridging the gap between open-ended analysis and cinematic storytelling. Generative AI was also used in the process of creating the game static assets (images, text, and music). name: Kipple
ai_disclosure: Kipple uses generative AI during play. A local language model produces creature dialogue and identity text, and a local image model paints creature artwork using the game's species, palette and trait recipes, including unusual hybrids. The resulting artwork is animated by the game's expressions, blinking, motion and elemental effects. The AI models and runtime come with the game and run on your PC. You do not need a personal AI subscription or API key. Memory uses locally stored conversation notes to provide context for later replies; your conversations do not alter the included models. Generation time and results vary with your hardware and may require another attempt. Conversations and creature memory files stay on your device in the included configuration. Steam authentication and inventory requests go online. Generated creature artwork, animated inventory images and item metadata are uploaded to Kipple's service for moderation and Steam inventory delivery; approved items can be visible to others through Steam inventory and eligible Community Market listings. Chat input and output are screened automatically. Recognised crisis messages receive a fixed, authored response pointing toward real-world help. Creature image prompts follow game-authored rules rather than free-form image requests. Generated items face additional server-side checks before Steam export. These checks reduce risk but cannot guarantee perfect output; AI replies can be inaccurate or inappropriate. Kipple is a fictional companion and does not provide professional advice. AI-generated artwork is also used in store and promotional materials, including electric-sheep key art, trailer thumbnails and the illustrated desktop wallpapers seen in trailers and screenshots. The scenery is desktop wallpaper: your companion lives over your own desktop.

ai_disclosure: Terran Dawn is a solo-developed game, and generative AI tools were used during its production. Everything AI-assisted is created ahead of time and shipped as fixed files inside the build: the game generates nothing while you play, contacts no AI service at runtime, and sends no player data anywhere. The game's design, story, missions, rules and balance are written by the developer. No generative AI runs while the game is playing.

ai_disclosure: A small language model (Google's Gemma 3 270M) runs entirely on the player's computer, with no network connection. It writes short lines of villager small talk, the ritual oracle's one- or two-sentence hint after a failed ritual, and routine filler records in the in-game archive, and it chooses which of our pre-written dialogue lines fits the moment. Guardrails: the player never types to the model — there is no text input anywhere in the game. Every prompt is a fixed template we wrote, filled in from game state such as a character's name, the time of day and the current quest. Output is short by construction (hard token caps, and lines over a few words are cut or discarded); lines that read as narration, stage directions or an assistant speaking are rejected; dialogue choices are constrained to our own authored lines. Any failure falls back to written lines. Players can turn the model off in Settings, and the game plays identically on written lines alone.

tags: Roguelike,Card Game,Word Game,Deckbuilding,Roguelike Deckbuilder,Indie,Spelling,Puzzle,Roguelite,Turn-Based Combat,Card Battler,Difficult,Atmospheric,Noir,Stylized,Dark Fantasy,Strategy,Perma Death,2D,Demons
ai_disclosure: Yes, Spell Death was made with AI. On purpose, out loud. Why? This is a game about a city that stopped reading. The demons here don't eat anyone. They need us. They keep the presses running, they copy everything and read nothing, and they are always hungry for more text. Sound familiar? I paid one to help me make this. Not made with AI: - The taste, the design, the systems and the balance. 10+ years of making mobile games and 30 years of collecting cards, building decks and theorycrafting. - The dictionary: a human-made list of about 196,000 words. (Even TRAGI. I still don't get TRAGI.) - Your words. Nothing is generated while you play. No suggestions, no autocomplete. There never will be. Made with AI: - Illustrations: image models, then picked, retouched and composed by hand. - Music: an AI music tool, directed by my taste for oriental and arabesque music and my obsession with the art deco and noir era. - Sound effects: most are synthesised from code, just math and stubbornness. A few come from the same AI music tool. - Code and some text: much of it drafted with an AI assistant, then edited, broken and fixed again by me. So I'm not standing outside the city pointing at it. I live here. A game about the trap, made from inside the trap. Art or hypocrisy, your call. (I've made mine.) The line, for me and for the game: a tool is fine, a proxy is not. The machine can draw a street. It doesn't get to do your reading, your thinking or your spelling. Still hate it? Fair. Spell something mean at it. It's a word game.
